# Cadenza v-next Spec — Fan-Out Review Report

*Generated by a multi-agent fan-out review (6 dimensions → adversarial per-finding verification → synthesis). 43 findings survived verification. This is a point-in-time review artifact, not part of the normative spec.*

> **Annotation (2026-07-03).** This is a historical, point-in-time artifact; its section names and
> framings reflect the spec **as reviewed on 2026-07-02** and some have since changed. In particular,
> finding #16 references the then-current interpreted-derivation-first model and headings
> (§"Two Modes Produce One Behavior"); the bootstrap was later reworked so the seed's derivation mode is
> compiled codegen and interpreted derivation is optional, and those headings were renamed. Read the
> current wording in `spec/bootstrap.md` and `spec/capabilities/self-hosting-and-bootstrap.md`, and the
> reworks in [bootstrap targets the compiler directly](./2026-07-03-bootstrap-targets-the-compiler-directly.md).
> Section references below are not updated, by design — a historical record is not rewritten.

## Verdict

The spec is genuinely coherent and unusually disciplined for a generation-0 tree: the frozen-contracts-first sequencing, the executable-semantics oracle plus dual gates, the RFC-2119 atomicity rules, and the learnings ADRs form a solid, self-aware backbone. But it is not yet sufficient for a downstream agent to derive a correct compiler: the "run" half of source→component→run is uncontracted (no export/entry model), and several core-semantics obligations the oracle and gates depend on — trap/terminal-condition, the observable-behavior projection, value equality, and the declarable type universe — are undefined or lean on undefined terms. A second, distinct class of gaps weakens the anti-gaming gate that the whole flywheel rests on (missing hivemind carve-outs for governance/optional-capability recording). Fix the semantics/runnability gaps and the gate-integrity gaps and the tree becomes buildable and trustworthy; the remaining items are discipline and polish.

## Cross-cutting themes

- End-to-end runnability is not closed: the component boundary pins imports exhaustively but leaves exports, the entry point, invocation input, and the typed host world unspecified, so the 'run' step has no contract.
- Core operational semantics the oracle/behavior-gate compare are under-defined: traps/terminal conditions, the observable-behavior projection (including emitted events), value equality/ordering, strings/collections, and the declarable type universe.
- Advertised capabilities outrun their requirement mass: verification layers (refinement, proof) and the #1 agent affordance (structural interface) are named as priorities but carry little or no enforceable/defaulted content.
- Gate integrity gaps let the anti-gaming machinery be gamed: no governance/change-process carve-out, no recording of the included/excluded optional-capability set, no immutable spec snapshot, and completeness/insensitivity checks that live as prose or SHOULD.
- RFC-2119 discipline slips: compound MUSTs, definition-in-disguise and expressibility requirements, and byte-identical duplicated sentences across files undermine the citation-identity model the gate relies on.
- Vocabulary and terminology drift: glossary omissions for normatively-used terms plus leftover pre-reboot phrasing ('surface', 'canonical tree').

## Ranked findings

### #1 — [BLOCKER] The component invocation contract (exports, entry point, and typed host world) is missing — source→component→run does not close

**Where:** spec/contracts/component-abi.md; spec/contracts/host-interface-binding.md; defaults/execution-model.md (cadenza-host/1 world)

**Problem:** Imports are pinned byte-for-byte (host-interface-binding mirrors the manifest), but nothing pins what a component EXPORTS: no requirement that a program has a designated entry, what the entry's input type/provenance is, how the runtime invokes it, or how that entry signature crosses the boundary. component-abi.md only speaks of 'an exported or imported signature' abstractly. Separately, the four host operations (read-projection/emit-event/read-blob/invoke-tool) exist only as one-line English prose with no typed signatures or WIT world. The ignition bar (bootstrap.md:67) requires a component to 'actually run to produce its output' and derivation-mode equivalence compares behavior 'over the same input,' yet neither the export it runs through nor 'the input' is defined. An agent generating the compiler must invent this convention, and overview §16 records that this exact 'component never materialized' failure is what the frozen-contract-first discipline exists to prevent — the import surface got a frozen contract while the export surface got none.

**Recommendation:** Add a frozen-contract section (component-abi.md or host-interface-binding.md) with technology-neutral requirements: (a) a derived component MUST export a defined entry; (b) a program's role MUST determine its entry signature; (c) the entry signature MUST lower/lift across the boundary per the component ABI; (d) tie 'the same input' in the oracle-agreement requirement to that entry. Then pin the concrete shapes in defaults/ (not in normative prose, per the standalone rule): add the fold-style entry signature and a typed cadenza-host/1 WIT world (each of the four ops' parameter/return/error shapes) in a default that host-interface-binding.md cross-references the way component-abi.md references type-mapping.md. Add a semantics/ignition case that runs a component through its export.

### #2 — [MAJOR] Runtime failure/trap semantics and the observable-behavior projection are undefined, though both are what the oracle and behavior gate compare

**Where:** spec/semantics/06-numeric-model.sexp (emits `(trap ...)`); spec/capabilities/numeric-model.md §Overflow Is Defined; spec/capabilities/core-semantics.md (no failure section); spec/glossary.md (Observable behavior; no trap term)

**Problem:** 'trap' appears as a corpus output and in defaults/numeric-model.md but is defined by no requirement and no glossary term: nothing states whether a trap halts the component, is observable, is deterministic, consumes fuel, is catchable, or how it serializes. numeric-model.md §Overflow Is Defined promises a 'defined, deterministic RESULT,' but the default resolves overflow to a trap — a control-flow EVENT, not a value — so requirement and realization describe different things. All partial operations (division by zero, Rational.of(_,0), out-of-bounds) are undefined. Meanwhile 'observable behavior' — the thing 'MUST agree with the reference interpreter' compares — is defined only in the descriptive glossary as 'the input-to-output relation and emitted events,' which omits the terminal condition (trap/fuel-exhaustion) and gives emitted events no representation in the corpus DSL, so two derivations could disagree on trap kind, event ordering, or halt point while both being 'correct.'

**Recommendation:** Add a normative failure-semantics section (core-semantics.md or a new capability): a trap deterministically halts the component at a defined point, is part of observable behavior, its relationship to the fuel-exhaustion halt, and whether it is representable/recoverable; enumerate the partial operations and give each a defined outcome. Promote a precise normative definition of the observable projection (final value in canonical value form; the ORDERED sequence of emitted events with content; the terminal condition normal/trap-of-kind-K/fuel-exhaustion; excludes internal representation, timing, diagnostics). Add an emitted-events clause to the corpus DSL. Reconcile §Overflow Is Defined to say 'defined deterministic OUTCOME' (allowing a trap) or introduce the trap concept it depends on.

### #3 — [MAJOR] Value equality/ordering and string/collection operational semantics are absent; a frozen contract leans on undefined 'equal' with a latent -0.0/NaN contradiction

**Where:** spec/contracts/deterministic-value-form.md:29-31,47; spec/semantics/01-literals.sexp (-0.0 kept distinct); defaults/hashing-and-encoding.md (byte-wise member order); no collections/strings/equality capability; spec/semantics/05-compound-types.sexp absent

**Problem:** The frozen deterministic-value-form contract requires 'two values the language considers equal MUST have identical canonical bytes' and 'distinct MUST have distinct bytes,' but equality is defined nowhere. This bakes in a contradiction: line 47 collapses NaN to one canonical form and the corpus keeps -0.0 distinct from 0.0, so under IEEE equality both frozen rules are violated, while under structural equality they hold — and nothing says which the language 'considers.' Ordering is never specified at the language level though the hashing default silently relies on byte-wise order. String semantics stop at 'stored in NFC' (no equality, length unit, indexing, comparison). Lists exist only in the type-mapping table; maps/sets are only implied by the value form; there is no collections capability and no 05-compound-types corpus.

**Recommendation:** Add capability requirements defining value equality (structural, with explicit float -0.0/NaN treatment reconciled to the value-form contract's equal-bytes rule), a total ordering where offered, and string text semantics (equality post-NFC, length unit, indexing, comparison). Add a collections capability (or expand core-semantics) covering list and map/set operations and their determinism, and write 05-compound-types corpus cases that witness construction, equality, and matching.

### #4 — [MAJOR] The declarable type universe (user-defined types, sum types, generics) has no requirements, though the ABI and inference presuppose it

**Where:** spec/capabilities/type-system.md (only static-typing/inference/soundness/erasure); spec/contracts/component-abi.md:38 (monomorphize generics); spec/capabilities/core-semantics.md:67 (match on scrutinee's type)

**Problem:** type-system.md's own Purpose says it 'defines the type universe' but it only requires that expressions have static types, that inference yields the most general type, and that types are erased. 'Most general type' presupposes polymorphism and the ABI requires monomorphizing generics, yet no requirement defines generics/type parameters, where they appear, or how they are bounded. The glossary defines nominal/structural/sum types and calls sum types 'the basis for typed results and error handling,' but no requirement governs declaring, constructing, or deconstructing them — and match exhaustiveness in core-semantics presupposes a sum-type variant set that is never normatively established. Since the requirement gate maps every normative sentence to impl+test, a divergent type language in this mandatory subsystem ships ungated.

**Recommendation:** Add type-system requirements (or a dedicated data-types capability): user-defined nominal and structural type declaration; sum-type declaration and its role in error handling; generics/polymorphism at the source level (placement, bounding, monomorphization before the boundary per component-abi.md); an explicit subtyping stance. Add 05-compound-types corpus cases witnessing declaration, construction, and matching.

### #5 — [MAJOR] The #1 agent affordance — the structural interface — is two abstract sentences with no declared default, uniquely among peer affordances

**Where:** spec/capabilities/agent-authoring.md §A Structural Interface Exists; defaults/ (no structural-interface.md); defaults/code-shape.md §requirements-this-choice-must-satisfy

**Problem:** Priority #1 rests on the structural interface, specified only as 'an interface exists to read and rewrite the canonical representation' and 'operate without re-parsing unrelated code.' AGENTS.md rule #7 requires a declared default for any point a conforming generation could resolve more than one way, and every peer affordance (execution-model, code-shape, diagnostics-schema, numeric-model, type-mapping, hashing, toolchain, bootstrap) has one — but there is no defaults/structural-interface.md. An agent doing structural generation needs a node-addressing scheme that survives edits, the closed set of edit operations, span↔node mapping, and query-by-kind/name; none exist even as defaults, and nothing requires node addressing to be stable/deterministic.

**Recommendation:** Add defaults/structural-interface.md pinning: a node-addressing scheme (stable path or content-derived id), the closed set of edit operations (insert/replace/delete/move), span↔node mapping, and query operations. Add requirements to agent-authoring.md that node addressing is a deterministic function of the representation and that a structural query result is reproducible, so an agent can target and re-target edits.

### #6 — [MAJOR] Gate integrity: no change-process/governance carve-out, so governance-floor and amendment MUSTs are either uncoverable or discharged by stubs

**Where:** constitution.md §Governance Floors and §Amendment Discipline; spec/capabilities/conformance-gate.md §Every Requirement Binds To An Enforcing Line, §The Gate Is The Promotion Bar; cf. hivemind conformance-gate.md §A Change-Process Requirement Is Not Load-Bearing For A Generation

**Problem:** constitution.md is an extracted [[specification]], so its Governance-Floor and Amendment MUSTs ('an amendment that weakens a governance floor MUST require explicit human approval', 'a change to the component ABI MUST be evaluated against already-derived components before it ships') are held load-bearing — but they describe acts on the spec/process, not runtime behavior a compiler performs, and conformance-gate recognizes only the impl+test citation kind. Hivemind hit this and added a carve-out plus enumerated the permitted enforcing-line KINDS (impl+test, governance-act citation, change-process-check citation) and pinned the non-load-bearing set at a declared default. Cadenza imported other hivemind learnings but not this one, leaving a dilemma: these MUSTs either block every promotion or get discharged by placeholder citations.

**Recommendation:** Port hivemind's section: a change-process/governance requirement is not load-bearing for a generation's runtime gate but still binds to an enforcing line elsewhere (governance-act or change-process check); pin the non-load-bearing set at a declared-default location so two builds judge against an identical load-bearing set; and enumerate the permitted enforcing-line kinds in §XV / conformance-gate rather than recognizing only impl+test.

### #7 — [MAJOR] Gate integrity: the included/excluded optional-capability set is not recorded, so a generation can shrink its load-bearing set unauditably

**Where:** spec/capabilities/conformance-gate.md §An Excluded Optional Capability Is Not Load-Bearing; per-capability §The Declared Default Is Include; cf. hivemind conformance-gate.md

**Problem:** A requirement of an EXCLUDED optional capability is not load-bearing, but nothing requires a gate run to record which optional capabilities were included/excluded, and nothing at the gate enforces the per-capability 'declared default is include' (it lives only inside each capability spec as build behavior). An adversarial generation can declare effect-tracking, verification-layers, property-based-testing, and units-of-measure all 'excluded,' drop dozens of MUSTs, pass on a smaller covered set, and — because no exclusion record is required — a reviewer re-running with the include-default gets a different load-bearing set and cannot reproduce or falsify the green result.

**Recommendation:** Add: a gate run MUST record which optional capabilities the build included so the load-bearing set is reproducible; and a build not told whether to include an optional capability MUST be judged as having included it (enforce include-by-default at the gate, not only in each capability spec). Pair with the rank-6 carve-out's pinned set so the whole load-bearing determination is reproducible.

### #8 — [MAJOR] Verification layers: refinement types and machine-checked proof are advertised priorities but have zero requirements

**Where:** spec/capabilities/verification-layers.md (whole); spec/overview.md §12

**Problem:** Priority #3 names three progressive layers — contracts, refinement types, machine-checked proof — but verification-layers.md contains only layer-agnostic discharge/optionality/certificate requirements. No requirement states a refinement invariant (admissibility, base↔refined coercion, meaning-preservation) or anything proof-specific (obligation statement, witness). Refinement appears normatively only as a test-generation constraint in property-based-testing.md; 'machine-checked proof' has no requirement, no glossary term, and is even absent from the planned 08-verification corpus file. So only contracts carry enforceable content, and the prose over-promises relative to requirement mass.

**Recommendation:** Either add invariant-level requirements for the refinement and proof layers (admissibility, base↔refined coercion, meaning-preservation, proof-obligation statement, reproducible witness checking) plus at least one semantics case each, or scope overview §12 down to the layers that actually have requirements and record refinement/proof as explicitly deferred open points in a defaults/ verification file.

### #9 — [MAJOR] Compound RFC-2119 sentences across the tree violate the atomicity rule the gate's citation-identity model depends on

**Where:** spec/capabilities/compiler-pipeline.md:32 (record diagnostic AND continue); constitution.md:104 (code AND span); spec/bootstrap.md:67 (derived AND run); spec/capabilities/property-based-testing.md:38 (terminate AND report minimal); spec/capabilities/conformance-gate.md:91 (list files AND hand-owned); spec/capabilities/self-hosting-and-bootstrap.md:62 (authored AND derivable, also definitional)

**Problem:** Multiple normative sentences join two independently satisfiable/violable obligations with 'and,' which AGENTS.md rule 1 explicitly forbids and the specs' own headers restate. Because a requirement's identity is (file, section, quoted sentence), one citation discharges both duties while a test sensitive to only one still passes — the exact failure the conformance gate warns about. compiler-pipeline.md:32 (record-diagnostic vs continue) is the most impactful; constitution.md:104 is even inconsistent with its own downstream spec (diagnostics.md already splits code and span into two atomic requirements).

**Recommendation:** Split each into one obligation per sentence. E.g. compiler-pipeline.md:32 → 'MUST record a diagnostic for that error.' + 'MUST continue processing the well-formed remainder rather than abort the whole compilation.' Apply the same mechanical split to constitution.md:104, bootstrap.md:67, property-based-testing.md:38, conformance-gate.md:91. For self-hosting-and-bootstrap.md:62, also drop the definitional 'MUST mean' form (Self-hosting is already defined in the glossary) and keep only the enforceable duties.

### #10 — [MAJOR] Anti-gaming enforcement is soft where it must be hard: corpus completeness is prose, insensitive-test detection is SHOULD, and no immutable spec snapshot is recorded

**Where:** spec/semantics/README.md §Authoring rules ('corpus is complete per capability'); spec/capabilities/conformance-gate.md §The Gate Should Detect An Insensitive Test (SHOULD), §A Citation Discharges Its Own Requirement (MUST), §The Requirement And Code Sides Are Separated; cf. hivemind §The Gate Judges Against The Immutable Specification

**Problem:** Three related soft spots let presence stand in for behavior. (1) 'Every behavioral requirement is witnessed by a case' — the property that makes the behavior gate meaningful — lives only as a README bullet and a deletable template comment, not a requirement; only 2 of 8 corpus files exist, so most capabilities have no witnessing case. (2) The anti-vacuous obligations are MUST on the author but the only mechanism that detects them is a SHOULD, so a conforming gate need not catch an insensitive test — the exact hivemind 309/309 pattern. (3) Nothing requires the gate to judge against a content-addressed snapshot of the spec or to record the snapshot hash a result was computed against, so a quietly-weakened spec can be regenerated to green with no tamper-evident record.

**Recommendation:** Promote corpus-witnessing to a normative requirement: every behavioral requirement in an included capability MUST be witnessed by at least one corpus case, and a generation whose corpus omits a witness for a load-bearing behavioral requirement MUST NOT be promoted. Elevate insensitive-test detection to MUST for the behavior-level subset (keep SHOULD only for the undecidable general case). Add requirements that a gate run judges against a content-addressed snapshot of the canonical spec tree and that the result records that snapshot hash.

### #11 — [MINOR] Glossary omissions and drift: normatively-used terms are undefined, and one entry still uses retired 'surface' vocabulary

**Where:** spec/glossary.md — no entries for capability-safety, macro, hygienic, effect/effect-tracking, scrutinee, aliasing; :132 'Executable semantics' still says 'surface construct'

**Problem:** The glossary preamble claims every normatively-used term is defined and AGENTS.md rule 3 requires adding a term before using it normatively, but several terms carry weight in MUST sentences without a definition: 'capability-safety' (a named guarantee in a Governance-Floor MUST), 'macro'/'hygienic', 'effect'/'effect tracking', 'scrutinee', 'aliasing'. Separately, after the reboot renamed 'surface construct' → 'language construct' everywhere and deleted the 'Surface' term, the 'Executable semantics' entry still reads '...for what every surface construct does.'

**Recommendation:** Add glossary entries for Capability-safety (parallel to Determinism), Macro, Hygiene/hygienic, Effect (and Effect tracking), Scrutinee, and Aliasing — or reword the requirements to use already-defined vocabulary. Change glossary.md:132 'surface construct' → 'language construct' to match constitution IX / overview §10 / core-semantics.md.

### #12 — [MINOR] Module system depth is under-determined: cyclic dependencies, cross-module init/eval order, and colliding imported names

**Where:** spec/capabilities/modules-and-namespaces.md (all sections)

**Problem:** The module capability covers explicit imports, explicit visibility, content-addressed resolution, and no-authority-from-resolution, but omits three decisions a compiler-generating agent must make: (1) whether intra-program cyclic module dependencies are permitted or rejected (content-addressing forbids cross-package cycles but not modules that compile together into one component); (2) the top-level initialization/evaluation order across modules and whether it is observable (derivation-order determinism is covered by reproducible-derivation, but runtime cross-module init order is not); (3) how a name imported from two modules that collide is resolved (rejected? qualified?) — lexical-scope rules cover nested shadowing but not two equally-near same-level imports.

**Recommendation:** Add requirements to modules-and-namespaces.md fixing the cyclic-dependency policy (reject, or a defined evaluation rule), the runtime top-level initialization/evaluation order as a deterministic function of source (and whether it is observable), and the resolution of colliding imported names.

### #13 — [MINOR] The code-as-data form the #1 customer emits, and the human display that is priority #2, are never illustrated; comment/doc handling is unaddressed

**Where:** defaults/code-shape.md §The default; spec/semantics/01-literals.sexp; spec/capabilities/agent-authoring.md §Canonical Form / §Machine-Readable Output

**Problem:** The central design bet is 'code as data,' yet the homoiconic display is never exhibited once (every example is the conventional ML/Rust display), and no requirement pins that the representation has a machine-readable serialization an agent can construct and submit as a derivation input (Machine-Readable Output covers only compiler OUTPUTS). Priority #2's human display is realized by one clause — a family name ('ML/Rust family...') — with no rendering of a function, match, module, or capability declaration. And nothing anywhere mentions comments or doc text, which collides with the canonical byte-identical round-trip and homoiconicity (comments are not evaluation nodes, so either they are first-class and the hash/semantics must account for them, or canonicalization silently erases human annotation).

**Recommendation:** In code-shape.md, show at least one worked example of BOTH displays (homoiconic and conventional) covering a function, a match, a module with a capability declaration, and an annotation. Add a requirement that the canonical representation has a machine-readable serialization an agent can read and construct, and that submitting a well-formed serialized representation is an accepted derivation input equivalent to its canonical textual projection. State where comments/doc live in the representation, whether they survive the round-trip, and whether they are semantically inert (e.g., doc attributes attached to definitions rather than free-floating comments).

### #14 — [MINOR] Enforceability slips: an 'expressibility' requirement and a definition-in-disguise no mechanism can bind to a line

**Where:** spec/contracts/build-tool-interface.md:53 ('MUST be expressible as providing a new tool...'); spec/capabilities/self-hosting-and-bootstrap.md:62

**Problem:** build-tool-interface.md:53 is a modal possibility claim about a hypothetical different-language tool, not a checkable property of any artifact this build produces; Principle XV forbids writing as a requirement a statement no mechanism can enforce on a line, and the architectural intent is already stated descriptively in overview §9. self-hosting-and-bootstrap.md:62 ('Reaching self-hosting MUST mean...') fixes a term's meaning already defined in the glossary rather than imposing a detectable obligation.

**Recommendation:** Restate build-tool-interface.md:53 as a checkable property of the root (e.g., 'A minimal load-verify-run root MUST NOT contain a compiler for any source language.') or move the aspiration to overview.md and drop the RFC-2119 phrasing. Move the self-hosting definition to the glossary/overview and keep only the enforceable duties (already present at lines 60/68/70).

### #15 — [MINOR] Byte-identical duplicated normative sentences across files create coupled citations and drift risk

**Where:** constitution.md, spec/bootstrap.md, spec/capabilities/self-hosting-and-bootstrap.md, type-system.md, host-interface-binding.md, capabilities-and-effects.md, compiler-pipeline.md, conformance-gate.md

**Problem:** Five distinct normative sentences appear byte-identical in 2–3 normative files (e.g. 'A compiled program's observable behavior MUST agree with the reference interpreter over the same input.' in constitution.md:130, self-hosting:34, bootstrap.md:49). Because identity is (file, section, quoted sentence), each copy is a separate requirement with independent citations; rewording one copy silently desynchronizes the others, which keep valid citations and do not co-invalidate.

**Recommendation:** For each duplicated behavior, keep the authoritative sentence in one home (the constitution or the owning contract) and have the other files reference it descriptively or state a genuinely distinct obligation. If intentional restatement is kept, add a traceability note pairing the copies so a reword of one flags the others.

### #16 — [MINOR] Every flywheel turn after genesis is under-exercised: ignition-only exercisers and a permanently-deferrable AOT path

**Where:** spec/bootstrap.md §Ignition Demonstrates A Real End-To-End Derivation (scoped to 'An ignition'); spec/capabilities/self-hosting-and-bootstrap.md §A Regeneration Is Derived, Gated, And Run, §Two Modes Produce One Behavior; defaults/bootstrap-strategy.md

**Problem:** The three strong exercisers (runs-to-produce-output, imports-mirror-manifest, byte-identical re-derivation) are written only for 'An ignition'; each later generation's obligation is merely 'derived, passed both gates, and ran' — a defense-in-depth asymmetry where the bespoke end-to-end acceptance demonstration is required once and thereafter relies on generic (mandatory but self-authored) gate coverage. Relatedly, compiled/AOT derivation is an optional optimization with interpreted as the declared default, so a lineage can remain interpreted-only forever and never exercise ABI lowering/lifting through a compiled program on the critical path.

**Recommendation:** Generalize the ignition-bar exercisers to every promoted generation (or reference them from the regeneration requirements) so each turn re-demonstrates imports-mirror-manifest and byte-identical re-derivation on a real derived-and-run component. Add a requirement that self-hosting (or a named milestone) MUST exercise compiled derivation of a program through the component ABI against the oracle at least once, so the AOT path is proven to materialize.

### #17 — [NIT] Leftover pre-reboot terminology and descriptive imprecision in the index and overview

**Where:** defaults/README.md:22,38 ('canonical-tree-plus-surface', 'surface family'); spec/overview.md:49 + spec/traceability.md:45 ('the canonical tree'); spec/overview.md §3 ('what is hashed'); source-tree-encoding↔representation link

**Problem:** The defaults index describes code-shape.md with the discarded 'canonical-tree-plus-surface decision, the surface family' model that code-shape.md itself replaced with 'a homoiconic canonical representation with decoupled displays.' The §3 heading still says 'the canonical tree' (glossary term is 'canonical representation'). overview §3 says the representation 'is what is hashed,' while the frozen contract hashes the canonical textual form of the source tree — imprecise though reconciled by the round-trip. And no requirement states that a source-tree file's contents ARE the canonical textual form of a module, leaving the identity chain with a silent join.

**Recommendation:** Rewrite defaults/README.md:22 to 'the homoiconic canonical representation, the set of decoupled displays, the canonical textual form, and the round-trip discipline' and change 'a different surface family' at :38 to 'a different display.' Consider renaming overview §3 heading (and the traceability §3 row) to 'the canonical representation.' Align overview §3 to say the hash is over the canonical textual form (a faithful projection of the representation). Optionally add one requirement that a file in a canonical source tree contains a module rendered in the canonical textual form.

## Quick wins

- glossary.md:132 — change 'surface construct' to 'language construct' in the 'Executable semantics' entry (one-word fix that removes the last retired-vocabulary leftover).
- spec/contracts/component-abi.md:9-10 — add 'and [overview §8](../overview.md)' so the header reads §5, §6, §8, matching both traceability tables (it is the lone contract header that under-lists its traced sections).
- constitution.md:170 — replace the named engine 'the requirement gate ([duvet](...))' with just 'the requirement gate', matching how overview §14 and the glossary already speak abstractly; pin the concrete engine only in defaults/.
- spec/capabilities/metaprogramming.md — move the termination sentence (:48) out from under '### Expansion Is Reproducible' into '### Expansion Terminates' or the existing '### Compile-Time Evaluation Is Bounded', so the heading describes its requirement.
- spec/semantics/06-numeric-model.sexp:33 — give the rational case a serialized value form in the output slot instead of the constructor call `(: (Rational.of 1 2) Rational)`, so its output matches the self-denoting-literal form of every other case.

## Strengths to preserve

- Frozen-contracts-first sequencing: the component ABI and deterministic value/fuel forms are frozen before the capabilities that depend on them — a direct, documented response to the overview §16 'component never materialized' failure.
- The executable-semantics corpus as a behavioral oracle, gated by execution rather than by shape, plus the dual requirement-gate/behavior-gate promotion bar, is a genuinely strong anti-gaming architecture.
- Rigorous RFC-2119 atomicity discipline (one obligation per sentence, standalone prose, no concrete engines in normative text) with the identity model (file, section, quoted sentence) — the compound-MUST findings are deviations from an otherwise well-held rule, not the norm.
- Bidirectional traceability (normative section ⇄ overview section) is near-perfectly maintained; the component-abi §8 gap is the sole exception among all contract headers.
- The declared-defaults pattern cleanly separates durable normative invariants from replaceable tech pins, and the learnings/ ADRs faithfully capture the hivemind gaming lessons the reboot is built around.
- Display-decoupled-from-representation is a coherent, well-articulated core design bet, and capability-honesty / imports-mirror-manifest give the capability-safety story a concrete, checkable spine.
